config.title: New Year's Eve in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: How Silvester in Berlin actually works: the Brandenburg Gate party, free viewing spots, fireworks rules, transport and the morning after.

items.q: Is there a big public fireworks show in Berlin on New Year's Eve?
items.a: **Not a citywide one.** The ticketed Brandenburg Gate party ends midnight with a short professional show, around seven minutes in recent winters. The real spectacle is private: thousands of legal amateur fireworks rising from every street between roughly 23:30 and 00:45.

items.q: How do I get into the Brandenburg Gate New Year party?
items.a: In recent winters entry was **free but ticketed**, around 20,000 places, doors from 21:30. Tickets have been released in early December on kulturprojekte.berlin and disappear quickly, so set a reminder for the first days of December and book immediately. Arrive before 23:00; expect airport-style bag checks with no glass and no own fireworks.

items.q: Where can I watch the New Year fireworks in Berlin for free?
items.a: The two classic shapes: a bridge in the middle of it, or a hill above it. **Modersohnbrücke and Oberbaumbrücke** in Friedrichshain fill by 23:00 with rockets rising all around; **Drachenberg** in Grunewald gives the whole-city panorama if you take the S-Bahn toward Heerstraße by 22:30 and climb the unlit path with a phone light.

items.q: Does Berlin public transport run all night on New Year's Eve?
items.a: **Yes.** U-Bahn lines run through the night about every 10 minutes, the S-Bahn ring about every 10 and the main S-Bahn lines about every 20, with trams and buses on a Saturday-style timetable. The Brandenburger Tor station is normally closed from the afternoon because of the party, so walk from Friedrichstraße or Potsdamer Platz.

items.q: Is New Year's Eve in Berlin safe, and is it okay with kids?
items.a: It is loud and slightly lawless rather than dangerous, but the street between **23:30 and 00:45** is no place for small children: close-range bangs, sparks and drinking crowds. Take an early dinner seating, let kids watch the early rockets, then watch midnight from a window. Firework ban zones with police checks cover a few hotspots, announced each December.
